requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. The navigation also has a 'Log out' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-001, repo-tests-p12-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), the INS dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p12-039), and the list is the service's signed-in landing page (repo-tests-p12-129). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a signed-in session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The real address book holds an organisation's records, so it needs an authenticated organisation; the prototype cannot express sign-in.
requirements.deltaNote: A signed-out request for an address book page lands on sign in and comes back to the page asked for (repo-tests-p12-127, repo-tests-p12-128), signed-out requests to /address-book and /address-book/add redirect to /auth/sign-in with the path as redirect (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011), and a session without an organisation gets 403 (repo-insfrontend-p2-002).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: The last recorded titles are 'Address book | Import notification service', '<name> | Import notification service' and 'Delete address | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037, trace-ins-fit-p3-047): a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix. No claim records the titles changing.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p2-003, repo-tests-p12-002, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro wording.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already shows 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications' (repo-tests-p12-003, repo-tests-p15-119), replacing the earlier 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' (repo-insfrontend-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-010).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) to /address-book/add, shown whatever the list holds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list always shows 'Add a new address' to /address-book/add (repo-insfrontend-p2-010, repo-tests-p12-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-013).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order puts adding first and filtering below it.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already reads heading, intro, 'Add a new address', the collapsible 'Filter addresses' section and then the tabs (repo-tests-p15-119), replacing the earlier order that put the search form between the intro and the button (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-010).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads with no search or Type filter applied, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design, so it opens and closes without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tucks filtering away behind one disclosure.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already holds the search and Type filter in a collapsible 'Filter addresses' section whose search field is hidden until it is opened, and it still opens with JavaScript off (repo-tests-p12-005, repo-tests-p12-006, repo-tests-p12-010, repo-tests-p15-119).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: The list's search control is a searchbox labelled 'Search' (repo-tests-p12-007, repo-tests-p15-119), replacing the earlier 'Search addresses' (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, trace-e2e-p15-023).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guides the search with a placeholder, not a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: The last recorded field carries a hint 'Search by name, town or city, postcode or country', passed where the input macro most likely does not render it, and no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p2-006); no claim records a placeholder on the search field (repo-tests-p12-007).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search'. It is a real submit button of the filter form, so pressing it, or pressing Enter in the search field, submits the form with or without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control, built so the page works without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: A real submit button named 'Search', and Enter in the search field, already submit the filter form, with JavaScript on or off (repo-tests-p12-007 to repo-tests-p12-009, repo-tests-p12-011, repo-tests-p15-120); nothing records the button as icon-only, and the last recorded button was a primary text button (repo-insfrontend-p2-007). The prototype's icon button is type=button and submits nothing (c-169).

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, the labels of the roles it holds, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) and its country name; a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches the whole visible row, so 'Ballymore' or a country finds the entry.
requirements.deltaNote: The search already matches a word inside address line 2 and inside the county whatever its case, matches a name, part of address line 1 and part of a country name, and finds an address by the name of a role it holds (repo-tests-p12-029 to repo-tests-p12-031, repo-tests-p12-081), over the case-insensitive, partial, literal, trimmed, live-addresses-only matching the service already had (repo-addressbook-p3-034 to repo-addressbook-p3-039, repo-addressbook-p3-067). The k6 suite's worst-case search still rests on the narrower name, town and postcode match (repo-perftests-p2-023).

requirements.statement: The address book's country filter is an exact, trimmed ISO alpha-2 code, ignored when blank, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with the search term by OR.
requirements.why: The locked contract and ruling cv-048 fix these semantics; nothing in Design Release 2.1 asks to change them.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven by the address book's AddressSearchIT and OperatorServiceTest (repo-addressbook-p3-064 to repo-addressbook-p3-066, repo-addressbook-p3-074, repo-addressbook-p3-075); the list request now carries the filter as country codes alongside the search term and the roles (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-012), the parameter's own name being the service's.

requirements.statement: The address book filter is a GET form to the address book list carrying the selected tab, the search and the chosen role, and the address book API filters the whole tab by the search and the role and returns 8 a page. The parameters that carry the tab, the search and the role, and the values the tab parameter takes, are the INS service's to name. Pressing the search button, or pressing Enter in the search field or on the Type select, submits the form; changing the Type select submits nothing by itself. The page works fully without JavaScript, and no script re-requests the list as the user types. The same holds locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters live across the whole category with no apply button, and the prototype wins on that look and feel; the real address book is paged on the server, a constraint that overrides only the prototype's way of holding every row in the page (c-169). Sam's 9 October ruling keeps these server-side filters and leaves parameter names to the INS service.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already reads the tab, the search, the role and the page from the request address, applies the role on the server only when the search is submitted, and works with JavaScript off (repo-tests-p12-073, repo-tests-p12-078, repo-tests-p12-079), and asking the API for a tab's roles returns exactly the addresses holding any of them (repo-tests-p12-060). The search parameter is still named q (repo-tests-p12-078), as the k6 suite reads it (repo-perftests-p2-022).

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active, the submitted list's results line counts the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'), and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the count true to what is shown while filtering and hides pagination unless the matches need it; nothing the server-paged constraint forces changes that (c-169).
requirements.deltaNote: A submitted role filter already narrows both the rows and the count, nine matches read 'Showing 1-8 of 9' then 'Showing 9-9 of 9', a filter that leaves two matches leaves no pagination, and no pagination shows when the results fit one page (repo-tests-p12-074, repo-tests-p12-076, repo-tests-p12-089, repo-tests-p12-028).

requirements.statement: The list is split into category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch'. The tabs are the Ministry of Justice sub navigation component, each a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with the selected one marked; the INS frontend adds the @ministryofjustice/frontend package at the same major version as the animals frontend. The query parameter that carries the tab, and its values, are the INS service's to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups addresses by what they are used for, and the roles an address holds are what put it in a group.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already offers the tabs as links inside a navigation named 'Address types' with the shown tab marked current, addressed by a tab parameter of the service's own naming, and following a tab works with JavaScript off (repo-tests-p12-049, repo-tests-p12-050, repo-tests-p12-053, repo-tests-p12-066); the roles an address holds are what decide its tab (ruling-ian-2026-11-06-p1-032). The earlier single untabbed table (trace-e2e-p15-026) is gone.

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses' or 'Branch addresses'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads each category's table.
requirements.deltaNote: Each tab already shows its own level-2 panel heading in exactly those words (repo-tests-p12-054).

requirements.statement: An address is listed on the one tab whose category holds the roles it has: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin and consignor; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer and place of destination; Branch holds branch addresses. Because an address's roles all come from one category, it is never listed on more than one tab, and the list API can be asked for one category's addresses. How the address record holds its roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists an organisation under each use it is held for, and the address book groups the roles it stores into the categories the tabs show.
requirements.deltaNote: Each tab already lists exactly the addresses holding any of its roles and no others, each of the six roles belongs to exactly one tab, and an address holding only the branch role is not listed on the Origin and Consignor tab (repo-tests-p12-055 to repo-tests-p12-057, repo-tests-p12-057-m1, repo-tests-p12-059, repo-tests-p12-064). The earlier untyped record (repo-insfrontend-p2-070, trace-e2e-p15-082) and filterless list (repo-addressbook-p3-046) are gone.

requirements.statement: With no tab chosen in the request, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.
requirements.deltaNote: Opening the list with no tab asked for shows Origin and Consignor, and an unknown tab falls back to it with all the tabs still shown (repo-tests-p12-051, repo-tests-p12-052).

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected tab as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps a search across tabs but not a type, which is per category.
requirements.deltaNote: Following another tab already keeps the search term and resets the Type filter to its placeholder, and submitting a filter leaves the tab the user was on selected (repo-tests-p12-068, repo-tests-p12-080).

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer; 'Branch Address' on Branch.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows a tab by the role an address is held for.
requirements.deltaNote: The filter is already a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is the empty 'Select one', offering only the current tab's own roles worded 'Place of Origin', 'Consignor', 'Place of Destination', 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Branch Address' (repo-tests-p12-069 to repo-tests-p12-072).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps an address when one of the roles it holds equals the choice; the list API takes the roles and the tab so the filter runs over the whole category on the server, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses. How the record and the API carry roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type matching, delivered over the real, paged book.
requirements.deltaNote: A submitted role filter already narrows the rows and the count, finds addresses that fall beyond the tab's first page unfiltered, and the API returns exactly the addresses holding a role asked for, every path still pinned to live addresses and the caller's organisation (repo-tests-p12-074, repo-tests-p12-075, repo-tests-p12-083, repo-addressbook-p3-027), the role filter running in the service before the page is cut (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-018). Consignee, Place of destination and Branch address are proven only through the API (repo-tests-p12-086).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows 'Showing <first>-<last> of <total>' (repo-insfrontend-p2-014, repo-tests-p12-012, trace-ins-fit-p2-015), carrying the test id the suites read it by (repo-tests-p12-013).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the same table whatever it holds.
requirements.deltaNote: A search that matches nothing already shows 'Showing 0 of 0' with the column headers kept and no rows, and no test holds the list to any empty-state message (repo-tests-p12-014, repo-tests-p12-014-m1, repo-tests-p13-083). The empty-book message 'You have no addresses yet.' is what the extract last recorded in its place (repo-insfrontend-p2-012, trace-ins-fit-p2-032).

requirements.statement: The list's filter holds the search field, the Type select and the search button and nothing else: a user clears a search by emptying the search field and submitting it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's filter has no clear control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link sits below the tabs, is the only link there when a search matches nothing, and returns to the tab that was searched keeping its Type filter and dropping the search term (repo-tests-p12-015 to repo-tests-p12-017, repo-tests-p15-119, repo-insfrontend-p2-013, repo-insfrontend-p2-015).

requirements.statement: On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what each address is used for.
requirements.deltaNote: A role-backed tab's table already has the headings Name, Type, Address, Country and Action in that order (repo-tests-p12-018), replacing the earlier Name, Address, Country and hidden Action with no Type column (repo-insfrontend-p2-016, trace-e2e-p15-026).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column, and Type reads 'Commercial' or 'Private'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows transporters by approval and type. The prototype reads the country off the last line of its one free-text address, which is its own data shape, so the real tab simply has no Country column.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab's table already has the headings Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Action, shows the transporter's approval number as given and names its type Commercial or Private (repo-tests-p12-019, repo-tests-p12-067, repo-tests-p12-088, repo-tests-p12-140). What the tab's Action column holds is unproven (repo-tests-p12-038).

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest; a one-word name stays on one line.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 breaks a listed name after its first word, which is look and feel the prototype decides, and the real list already does it.
requirements.deltaNote: A row's Name cell already shows the name's first word on its own line and the rest on a second, with a one-word name on one line (repo-tests-p12-032).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the whole address, line by line.
requirements.deltaNote: A row's Address cell already shows each stored line on its own line, every line but the last ending in a comma, and leaves out the lines the record does not hold (repo-tests-p12-033), replacing the earlier one-line join of address line 1, town or city and postcode (repo-insfrontend-p2-018, trace-e2e-p15-027).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The Country cell shows the country's name (repo-tests-p12-034, repo-insfrontend-p2-019, trace-e2e-p15-028).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the labels of the roles the address holds, joined by ', ', using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination' and 'Branch'. These differ in case and wording from the Type filter's options.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels uses in sentence case in the table.
requirements.deltaNote: A row's Type cell already names the roles the address holds, joined by a comma and a space, worded Place of origin, Consignor, Place of destination, Consignee, Importer and Branch (repo-tests-p12-062, repo-tests-p12-063).

requirements.statement: Each row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action; the hidden name keeps each link distinct for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: Each row's action is already a link named 'View <the record's name>' that opens that record's own page, and it is the only row action (repo-tests-p12-036, repo-tests-p12-037, repo-tests-p15-121, repo-insfrontend-p2-020).

requirements.statement: The address book list shows 8 addresses a page, asked for through the list API's page-size parameter, which runs from 1 to 100 and defaults to 25.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages at 8, and the address book's list API takes the page size as a request parameter within those bounds, so the INS list asks for 8 without changing the contract's default.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already shows eight addresses a page with the rest on the next page, and re-counts the rows as the user pages (repo-tests-p12-020, repo-tests-p12-021); eight is the figure the INS address book list uses (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-035-m1, ruling-ian-2026-11-23-p1-003), and the page size runs from 1 to 100 defaulting to 25 (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-015, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-017). The earlier 25 a page (repo-addressbook-p3-011, trace-ins-fit-p2-023, trace-e2e-p15-030) is gone.

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; with one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already renders GOV.UK pagination as a navigation named 'Pagination' with 'Page <n>', 'Next page' and 'Previous page' links, marks the current page, collapses page numbers with an ellipsis over five pages, and shows none when the results fit one page (repo-tests-p12-022 to repo-tests-p12-024, repo-tests-p12-028, repo-insfrontend-p2-021). Paging backwards is not proven (repo-tests-p12-025).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the user's tab and filters as they page.
requirements.deltaNote: The next-page link already keeps the tab, the search term and the role filter and adds the page, and following it keeps the tab selected and the role filter chosen (repo-tests-p12-026, repo-tests-p12-027).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty page for a stale page link.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing, non-numeric or sub-1 page already means page 1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-011, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-014), but a page beyond the last gets an empty items list from the API (repo-addressbook-p3-017) while only the label and pagination are clamped (repo-insfrontend-p2-023).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists the user's latest additions first; the real API already sorts newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: The API sorts by creation time, newest first, ties by id (repo-addressbook-p3-028, repo-addressbook-p3-029, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013); an address just added is listed ahead of an older one matching the same search (repo-tests-p12-035, trace-e2e-p15-031).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already shows an add, edit or delete message once in a GOV.UK 'Success' notification banner, gone after a reload (repo-tests-p12-040, repo-tests-p12-042, repo-tests-p12-043, repo-tests-p12-047, repo-insfrontend-p2-028, repo-insfrontend-p2-029). The add and edit banner wording belongs to the add-and-edit area.

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page until the user leaves or reloads it, and no script hides it on a timer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's banner stays until the user moves on, so slower readers do not miss it, and WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer.
requirements.deltaNote: A success banner is still showing ten seconds later and goes only when the page is reloaded (repo-tests-p12-043); the script that hid it after 3 seconds (repo-insfrontend-p2-030) is gone.

requirements.statement: After a delete the list's success banner reads '<name> address deleted', with the address's name as the user entered it, or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: A completed deletion already returns to the list with the banner '<name> address deleted' (repo-tests-p12-044, repo-tests-p13-082), replacing '<name> deleted from your address book' (repo-insfrontend-p2-031, trace-e2e-p15-035). The blank-name wording is unproven, and whether the name is re-cased is c-367's question.

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and organisation scoping are real constraints the prototype, which holds the book in one user's session, cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The service scopes by organisation only, with no user identity (repo-addressbook-p4-003, repo-tests-p12-123); an address one user adds is found by another user of the same organisation, and one a user deletes is gone for them (repo-tests-p12-124, repo-tests-p13-091, trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-172: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403.
requirements.why: Organisation isolation and non-disclosure are real authorisation constraints (rulings cv-010 and cv-040).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in the address book's AddressScopingIT and IdentityHeaderFilterTest (repo-addressbook-p4-053, repo-addressbook-p4-054, repo-addressbook-p4-059) and end to end against a fresh organisation created for each test, where a user asking for another organisation's address is returned to the list without being shown its name (repo-tests-p12-125, repo-tests-p15-127-m1); no spec asserts the status code or refusal message behind that landing (repo-tests-p12-126).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's only tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter enforces it on every /organisation/ path (repo-addressbook-p4-006, repo-addressbook-p4-010, repo-addressbook-p4-044), and every address book call the suites make carries it (repo-tests-p12-123).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation.
requirements.why: The address book trusts the header alone, so it must come only from the authenticated session (ruling cv-010).
requirements.deltaNote: The INS client sets the header from the session and fails before sending without one (repo-insfrontend-p2-065, repo-insfrontend-p2-067), and the book is addressed per organisation under that path (repo-tests-p12-123, trace-e2e-p15-080).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests without the search term, and times the list endpoint and its query as metrics.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter and OperatorController already do this (repo-addressbook-p4-036, repo-addressbook-p3-048, repo-addressbook-p3-049).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The real list contract the INS frontend reads.
requirements.deltaNote: OperatorPageResponse and OperatorListIT (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-addressbook-p3-053); asking with no role returns every live address of the organisation (repo-tests-p12-061) and the endpoint lists the caller's live addresses newest first, one page at a time (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications keep referring to addresses after they are deleted, so deletion must stay detectable.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressGetIT proves 200 with deleted true for a tombstone and 404 for an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p2-033, repo-addressbook-p2-034), and a deleted record stays readable by its id marked deleted with its name intact (repo-tests-p12-134, repo-tests-p13-081).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 removes the address from the book; the tombstone is the real persistence constraint that stops notifications referencing it from dangling.
requirements.deltaNote: The service soft-deletes and answers 204 idempotently (repo-addressbook-p2-053, repo-addressbook-p2-058); a deleted address is no longer found by a search for its name but stays readable by id marked deleted (repo-tests-p12-046, repo-tests-p13-081, repo-tests-p13-090, trace-e2e-p15-075).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The address details page is served at /address-book/<address id> with the address's own name as its level-1 heading (repo-tests-p13-066, repo-insfrontend-p2-032, repo-insfrontend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on these rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page shows these rows in this order (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-tests-p13-067, trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: An address holding neither an address line 2 nor a county already shows neither row, leaving seven (repo-tests-p13-068), where both rows once always showed blank (repo-insfrontend-p2-049, trace-ins-fit-p2-041).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label, and the V4 Address Block gives every address block a County field.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page's county row already reads 'County (optional)' (repo-tests-p13-067), where it once read 'County' (repo-insfrontend-p2-045, trace-ins-fit-p2-042).

requirements.statement: The view page does not show the roles the address holds, and its summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page lists nine summary rows with no roles row and no Change links (repo-tests-p13-067, repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-insfrontend-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 styles Edit as secondary.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page offers Edit as a link styled as a button to /address-book/<id>/edit (repo-tests-p13-069), and the last recorded styling is primary (green) rather than secondary (repo-insfrontend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page has a warning 'Delete' button-link to /address-book/<id>/delete (repo-insfrontend-p2-052, repo-tests-p13-069, trace-ins-fit-p2-045).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page's Back link goes to /address-book when no return is carried, and also when the return names a page on another frontend (repo-insfrontend-p2-091, repo-tests-p13-071, trace-ins-fit-p2-047).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return is honoured when it starts with a single / (an INS page), or when it is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opened the address from a journey page of either animals set (live-animals or germinal-products, both in the animals frontend) goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). The return parameter's name is the INS service's to choose. Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from; the animals frontend is on another origin, a cross-service constraint that extends the prototype's single-/ rule to that one origin and never to any origin (c-170).
requirements.deltaNote: An INS return path is already honoured throughout: Back follows it, Edit and Delete carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it, a completed delete lands on it, and a return naming the deleted address's own pages falls back to the list (repo-tests-p13-069, repo-tests-p13-070, repo-tests-p13-085 to repo-tests-p13-087). A return naming a page on another frontend is ignored (repo-tests-p13-071), so nothing yet honours an absolute animals frontend return, and the INS frontend is addressed by its own base URL (repo-tests-p15-128).

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects a dead address link instead of showing an error.
requirements.deltaNote: An unknown id goes to the return or the list, and a malformed id, another organisation's address and a deleted address each return to the list without showing a name (repo-tests-p13-072 to repo-tests-p13-075), where all three once answered 404 (repo-insfrontend-p2-033, repo-insfrontend-p2-035, repo-insfrontend-p2-036).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats a stale delete as a no-op rather than an error.
requirements.deltaNote: A delete page opened for an unknown or already-deleted id returns to the list, and confirming a deletion for an address deleted meanwhile changes nothing and shows no banner (repo-tests-p13-088 to repo-tests-p13-090), where both once answered 404 (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-173: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list renders the shared recoverable error banner with no table, and the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list renders 'There is a problem' on failure and the view and delete pages respond 500 (repo-insfrontend-p2-025, repo-insfrontend-p2-037, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The list renders in the wide display column; the view and delete pages in the two-thirds column; every page keeps the skip link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: Today's layout; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p2-027 and repo-insfrontend-p2-038-m1 set the columns; trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 shows the footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a legal requirement for the service.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS fit suite runs axe on each page and passes (repo-insfrontend-p2-085, repo-insfrontend-p2-092, repo-insfrontend-p2-096), and the tests repo's accessibility specs drive the list and delete pages in their current form (repo-tests-p15-118, repo-tests-p15-119).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; Design Release 2.1 overrides only this address book view.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete confirmation page is served at /address-book/<address id>/delete and posts to itself (repo-insfrontend-p2-053, repo-tests-p13-076).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page is headed 'Delete this address?' (repo-tests-p13-076, repo-tests-p15-118), where it once read 'Delete address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-054, trace-ins-fit-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what is being deleted before the user confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page already summarises the address in one row keyed 'Address' holding the name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode and the country in words, and leaves out the email and phone (repo-tests-p13-077, repo-tests-p13-077-m1, repo-tests-p13-077-m2), where it once showed only the name (repo-insfrontend-p2-056). The 'Not applicable' fallback is unproven.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; the name now shows in the summary.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page reads 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.' (repo-tests-p13-078), where it once asked 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' (repo-insfrontend-p2-055, trace-ins-fit-p3-048).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the user; it is true, as the API has no restore.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the warning reads 'Deletions are permanent and you cannot undo this.' (repo-tests-p13-079, repo-tests-p15-118) rather than the design's wording.

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button text.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page's confirm control reads 'Yes, delete' (repo-tests-p13-080, repo-tests-p15-118), where it once read 'Yes, delete this address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-059, trace-ins-fit-p3-050).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers cancel as a link, not a second button.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page's controls are a 'Yes, delete' button and a 'No, cancel' link, and cancelling returns to the address's own details page, deletes nothing and shows no banner (repo-tests-p13-080, repo-tests-p13-084, repo-tests-p12-045), where cancel was once a secondary submit button (repo-insfrontend-p2-060, trace-ins-fit-p3-051).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the delete page's Back link goes to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page's Back goes to /address-book/{id} (repo-insfrontend-p2-057, repo-tests-p13-085).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete deletes the address through the address book service and, with no return path, lands on the list, which shows no row for that address and counts one fewer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: A completed deletion returns to the address book list with the deleted banner, and the address is no longer found there (repo-tests-p13-082, repo-tests-p13-083, repo-insfrontend-p2-061, trace-e2e-p15-074).

requirements.statement: The delete form is protected by a CSRF token and posts nothing else.
requirements.why: A real security constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete form carries a crumb token and posts nothing else (repo-insfrontend-p2-058, trace-ins-fit-p3-068, repo-perftests-p2-037).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address makes no check on whether a notification uses it and shows no in-use warning.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; the tombstone keeps those notifications' references whole.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete proceeds unconditionally (repo-insfrontend-p2-109).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's in-memory address book stub behaves like the real list: 8 a page, filtering by search, tab and role, and soft-deleting so a deleted address reads back as deleted.
requirements.why: The fit suite runs against the stub, so it must exercise the list the design asks for rather than an unfiltered one.
requirements.deltaNote: The last recorded stub pages at 25, ignores the search term and country code, and deletes outright (repo-insfrontend-p2-078, repo-insfrontend-p2-079, repo-insfrontend-p2-081), so no fit test can cover searching (repo-insfrontend-p2-106).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, kept marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The INS frontend carries Welsh copy for every address book string; leaving the old Welsh would show users a different page in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: The last recorded Welsh copy matches the older English: 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau', 'Dileu cyfeiriad' and so on (repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to repo-insfrontend-p2-105), and no claim records Welsh for the tabs, the Type filter or the new delete wording.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry the roles the add flow offers, so they land on the right category tab and the journey parties still find them, and the pre-run reconcile treats a missing or drifted role as drift.
requirements.why: Once the list is split by role, roleless fixtures would sit on no tab and the E2E specs that find them would break.
requirements.deltaNote: The shared organisation's fourteen fixtures each hold roles, every one shows on the tab that holds its role, and seeding rewrites a record whose details or roles differ while leaving a correct one untouched (repo-tests-p12-112, repo-tests-p12-113, repo-tests-p12-065, repo-tests-p12-115, repo-tests-p12-116, repo-tests-p12-117-m1).

requirements.statement: End-to-end specs reach the address book's view and delete pages through its own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete'), and cover the empty and no-match state.
requirements.why: A spec that opens a page by its URL proves nothing about whether a user can get there.
requirements.deltaNote: The suite now opens the list, follows a tab link, searches within it and opens a record by its View link, reaching Delete from the record's own page, and a search matching nothing is covered (repo-tests-p12-141, repo-tests-p12-036, repo-tests-p12-037, repo-tests-p12-008, repo-tests-p12-014, repo-tests-p12-045).

requirements.statement: The prototype's seeded demonstration addresses (its farms, transporters, three Defra branches, multi-type entries and padding copies) and their ids.
requirements.why: Demonstration data: the real book holds each organisation's own records.

requirements.statement: DR1's own address book screens and the animals frontend's navigation into them.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements (the ruling), and inc-062 struck DR1's address book screens; Design Release 2.1 governs the INS book's design.

requirements.statement: Closing the address book service's own test gaps: no test proves the country filter is case-sensitive, nor that the search term leaves out phone and email.
requirements.why: A test-coverage gap in a contract this programme does not change; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: The address book list page shows the service's Alpha phase banner, 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', with its feedback link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the Alpha banner on the address book list, and the INS layout already carries it.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS shared layout already renders an Alpha phase banner with that text and an email feedback link (trade-imports-ins-frontend src/server/app/shared/layout.njk and copy.en.js phaseBanner, read at reconcile; no claim in this area's working set records it).

requirements.statement: The roles an address can hold read, in order, with these hints: 'Place of Origin' ('The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'), 'Consignor' ('This is the sender of the consignment.'), 'Consignee' ('This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'), 'Importer' ('This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'), 'Place of Destination' ('This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'), then, after a divider, 'Branch Address' ('This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's address type list is the wording for the six roles an address can hold, and it also names the categories the list's tabs and Type filter group by; the choice itself is made on the add-and-edit area's roles step.
requirements.deltaNote: The six roles already exist (repo-tests-p12-091, ruling-ian-2026-11-16-p1-007) and the add and edit forms word them 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Place of destination', 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Branch address' (repo-tests-p12-085), in sentence case rather than the design's title case, grouped per address type rather than in one list with a divider (repo-tests-p12-144), and no claim records a hint against any of them.

requirements.statement: The INS address book offers everything the k6 performance suite reads from it: the list at /address-book with the heading 'Address book', a search by the q parameter, each row's link to /address-book/<id>, the view page at /address-book/<id> showing the address's name, the delete confirmation at /address-book/<id>/delete whose form posts nothing but the CSRF token, a 200 landing after the delete with no link to the deleted address, and the results line marked data-testid 'address-book-results-label'.
requirements.why: The address book changes keep every route and hook the k6 suite uses: no increment changes a real URL path, and the search parameter is the INS service's to name, so it keeps q. The suite changes only where a row breaks one of its scripts (c-225).
requirements.deltaNote: The k6 suite already requests these routes and reads these hooks against the INS address book (repo-perftests-p2-020 to repo-perftests-p2-022, repo-perftests-p2-033, repo-perftests-p2-034, repo-perftests-p2-037, repo-perftests-p2-038, repo-perftests-p2-046), the search parameter is still q and the results line still carries that test id (repo-tests-p12-078, repo-tests-p12-013).

requirements.statement: The k6 performance suite's address book scenarios work against a list split into category tabs: the setup search that makes sure 'Perf Test Holding' exists, each address-book session's search for the address it has just added, and the worst-case search each ask for the tab their address's roles land on; the background-volume count adds up every tab's results line, its seeded addresses each carrying one role so none is counted twice; and the suite leaves nothing behind in the book.
requirements.why: A search and a results line that cover only the selected tab make a search on the default tab miss an address of another role, so setup would add a duplicate or fail and the book count would be one tab's. The suite changes in the row that breaks it, because the 7 October ruling works out which repos change from the evidence (c-225).
requirements.deltaNote: The k6 suite still searches the whole book with q and reads the whole book's count from the results line (repo-perftests-p2-039, repo-perftests-p2-046), while the list is now addressed per tab (repo-tests-p12-053).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, the address book list re-requests itself as the user types in the search field or changes the Type select (debounced), and swaps in the table, the results line and the pagination without a full page load, with no apply button, enhancing the GET form that already works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design dropped it on 13 November: address search does not filter as the trader types, so there is nothing to build; the trader presses Search or Enter, which the list already does (req-1121, req-1122).
requirements.deltaNote: The list changes only when the filter form is submitted (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-tests-p12-073).

requirements.statement: The address book list has a 'Transporter' tab, between 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Branch', headed 'Transporter addresses', listing the organisation's transporter records, and the tab has Welsh copy.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has a Transporter category in the address book, and the address book is the service of record for transporters, so the tab is backed by the transporter records rather than by a seventh address role.
requirements.deltaNote: The 'Transporter' tab, its 'Transporter addresses' panel heading and its transporter rows are already built, listing transporters rather than addresses with roles (repo-tests-p12-049, repo-tests-p12-054, repo-tests-p12-058, repo-tests-p15-129); no claim records Welsh copy for the tab, which the 9 October afternoon ruling left waiting with transporter management until ruling:ian-2026-11-06 settled that the address book manages transporters.

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the Type filter offers 'Select one', 'Commercial' and 'Private', and keeps a transporter whose type equals the choice, filtered on the server over the whole tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters transporters by their type, which is intrinsic to the transporter record rather than a role.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab's Type filter already offers Select one, Commercial and Private in that order and a Commercial filter narrows eleven matches to two, finding transporters beyond the first page and leaving no pagination (repo-tests-p12-087, repo-tests-p12-089, repo-tests-p15-129). Private is never chosen in a test (repo-tests-p12-090).

requirements.statement: The address type question offers a 'Transporter' option, third and before 'Branch', with the hint 'This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.', and choosing it opens the transporter pages, which ask no roles.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers a Transporter address type, and the address book now manages transporters, so the option has somewhere to lead.
requirements.deltaNote: The question already offers Transporter third, before Branch, and choosing it opens its own pages and carries no roles (repo-tests-p12-053, repo-tests-p12-143), but its hint reads 'Private, Commercial' rather than the design's wording (repo-tests-p15-130).

requirements.statement: On the address book list the delete success banner shows the address's name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and its driving spec both put the name in sentence case in this banner, but no source says why, and the real book holds names the user typed, where lower-casing the rest reads as a mistake on 'Alpine Dairy GmbH' or 'Animal and Plant Health Agency'.
requirements.deltaNote: The banner shows the name as it is stored, unchanged (repo-insfrontend-p2-031, trace-e2e-p15-035); the banner assertion is templated on the record's own name, so nothing proves the case either way (repo-tests-p12-044), and the shared fixtures include names such as 'Alpine Dairy GmbH' (repo-tests-p12-112).

requirements.statement: When the request carries a search or a Type, the address book list's 'Filter addresses' disclosure is open as the page loads, showing the search term and the type the results are filtered by.
requirements.why: The prototype filters in the browser, so its list never loads with a filter already applied and its design says nothing about that case; filtered on the server, a disclosure that is always collapsed hides the term and type the results rest on.
requirements.deltaNote: The search field is hidden until the disclosure is opened (repo-tests-p12-005), and nothing records what the disclosure does when the request already carries a search or a role.

requirements.statement: The delete page's Address row leaves out any line that repeats one already shown, ignoring case.
requirements.why: The prototype holds a seeded address as one free-text string whose last part is its country, so it has to drop the repeat; the real record holds separate lines and an ISO country code looked up to a name, so no line repeats another, and dropping a line the user typed would hide part of what is being deleted.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page lists every part of the record's address in its one row (repo-tests-p13-077).

requirements.statement: The address book list groups and labels the address types 'consignor or exporter', 'exporter', 'contact' and 'packer'.
requirements.why: These four types exist only in the prototype's seeded demonstration data, which maps the service's own consignment and contact addresses into the book. The address book's role vocabulary is six roles, no exporter role exists and none is to be created, the roles question does not offer these four and the prototype's own Type filter gives them no option, so the real book never holds one; building a category membership and a column label for each would be dead work.

requirements.statement: Search also matches a transporter's approval number, so a trader finds a transporter by the number on its approval.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches a transporter's whole row, its approval number included, and the approval number is the identifier a trader is given.
requirements.deltaNote: A transporter row shows its approval number (repo-tests-p12-067, repo-tests-p12-140), but no claim records a search matching one, and the address search matches only an address's own fields (repo-addressbook-p3-032).

requirements.statement: Every list of an organisation's addresses is served and shown a page at a time: the address book's list API takes a 1-based page number defaulting to 1 and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, and no caller is served an organisation's whole address book in one answer.
requirements.why: Organisations in the test environments hold thousands of addresses, so a list without paging makes the service struggle; the owner's ruling of 25 November keeps paging everywhere and withdraws the earlier reading that the role-scoped list is served unpaginated.
requirements.deltaNote: The list endpoint already takes the page and page size within those bounds and lists the caller's live addresses one page at a time (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-011, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-014, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-015, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-017, repo-addressbook-p3-005, repo-addressbook-p3-012), and the list shows eight a page (repo-tests-p12-020).

requirements.statement: The address book's list API takes the roles an address must hold, repeatable so that holding any one of them is enough, and separately the roles a search term is widened by, so an address holding one of those roles matches a text search even when its own text does not; both filters run in the service, alongside the organisation scope and the live-addresses-only rule, before the page is cut.
requirements.why: The list's tabs and Type filter cover a whole category, so one request must be able to ask for several roles at once and the filter must run before paging, or a page of results would be wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: Asking the API for a tab's roles returns exactly the addresses holding any of them, asking for one role returns exactly the addresses holding it and nothing for a role no address holds, and a search role widens a text search so an address holding it matches while one holding neither is left out (repo-tests-p12-060, repo-tests-p12-083, repo-tests-p12-084); the endpoint takes the roles and search roles alongside the page and page size, and the role filter runs before the page is cut (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-016, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-018).

requirements.statement: An address saved through the address book is found by the next search of the address book list straight away.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the tests repo has to wrap the first search after a save in a retry until it passes, so the list's search lags behind a write. Read-after-write consistency in the address book's own store is not a Design Release 2.1 look-and-feel difference and this programme does not fix it, so it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the suite wraps the first search after a save, and the walk through its result pages, in a retry that runs until it passes (repo-tests-p12-082-m1).

conflicts.about: Address book page size, and whether the page size can be asked for at all: Design Release 2.1's 8 against the server-set 25 and ruling cv-025's 'page size is configuration, not a request parameter'.

positions.says: The list shows 8 addresses a page.
The list shows 8 addresses a page.
The list endpoint's page-size parameter runs from 1 to 100 and defaults to 25, and the INS address book list already uses eight.
The list API pages with page and pageSize, pageSize being 1 to 100 and defaulting to 25.
The list takes no page-size parameter: the page size is set on the server, defaulting to 25.
Ruling cv-025: the page size is server-side configuration, not a request parameter.
The page size is read from the address-book.list.page-size setting and is 25 when that setting is absent.
The INS list shows 25 addresses a page.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins on the figure: 8 a page (req-1141). The owner's rulings of 5 and 25 November settle how it is asked for: the list API takes the page size as a request parameter running 1 to 100 and defaulting to 25, so the INS frontend asks for 8 and the contract's default is untouched (req-address-book-list-001). Ruling cv-025's reading that the page size could only be server configuration, and that the endpoint takes no page-size parameter, are set aside; the 25 the service once served with no setting stays as the evidence of what changed.

conflicts.about: How filtering works: the prototype holds every row of a category in the page and filters it in the browser as the user types; the real list is served one server-sized page at a time by the address book API; Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling holds filtering as the user types until design answers, and design then dropped it.

positions.says: The search button does not submit; a client-side module filters every entry the page carries as JSON.
Typing sends no request, so all a category's rows must already be in the page; pagination hides while filtering.
The list is paged on the server and cannot be asked for everything.
Search is a GET form submitted with a Search button, answered by the API's q.
The ruling does not say whether, where a real constraint overrides, the service keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as it can.
inc-067 to inc-069's server-side filters are kept (c-169).
Filtering as the trader types is not built until design answers question 5; search on the Search button or Enter is built now, and the filter is a GET form the button or Enter submits.
Address searching is built without live filtering: the search does not filter as the trader types, on the address book list included.

conflicts.outcome: Search on the server, without JavaScript. The filter stays a GET form to the address book list carrying the tab, the search and the role; the address book API filters a whole tab by the search term (over the widened fields) and the role and returns 8 a page. The search button is a real submit button, and pressing it or Enter submits the form; while filtering, the results line counts the matches and pagination shows only when the matches run past 8 (req-1118, req-1121, req-1122). Same locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP. Design's ruling of 13 November closes the question Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling opened: the list does not filter as the trader types, so the JavaScript half is dropped rather than deferred (req-2039). The prototype's mechanism of loading a category's every address into the page as JSON, filtering in the browser and a search button that submits nothing is set aside: the real book is paged on the server, and every page must work without JavaScript. Sam's 9 October ruling keeps these server-side filters and leaves the names of the tab and search parameters to the INS service (c-253).

conflicts.about: Return paths into the address book: the prototype's return query is a same-site path, but in the real service the pages that link into the book with a return (the animals journey) are on another origin.

positions.says: A return path is honoured only when it starts with a single /; anything else falls back to the list.
The INS frontend is addressed by its own base URL, separate from the animals frontend and the plants frontend, and a return naming a page on another frontend is ignored.
The view page's Back always goes to the address book list.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype's return query is adopted, shaped by the cross-origin constraint: INS honours a return that starts with a single / as an INS page, as the prototype does, and an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opens an address from an animals journey page goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured. The always-back-to-the-list behaviour is replaced, and the single-/ half is already built (req-1167).

conflicts.about: Controls and states the INS list had that Design Release 2.1 does not: the empty-state and no-match messages, the Clear search link and the banner that hides itself.

positions.says: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1, it changes to match.
When nothing matches the list shows an empty table and 'Showing 0 of 0', with no message.
The filter's only button is the search icon; there is no clear control.
The success banner is shown once and cleared, with no timed hide.
An empty book shows 'You have no addresses yet.'
A search with no match shows 'No addresses match "<term>".' and a Clear search link.
A 'Clear search' link sits below the tabs, is the only link there when a search matches nothing, and returns to the tab that was searched keeping its Type filter.
The success banner hides itself after 3 seconds.
The address book's success banner stays, and the INS frontend's script that hides it is removed.

conflicts.outcome: The rulings and the prototype outrank the INS frontend and the tests repo: these are differences from Design Release 2.1 and none rests on persistence, validation, authentication or cross-service behaviour, so they go. The banner and the no-match message have already been put right (req-1132, req-1147), while the Clear search link has survived into the built list and still has to come out (req-1133). The 7 October ruling's own open point on behaviour Design Release 2.1 does not show at all does not apply: the prototype shows its empty, search and banner states. The repo and tests claims are not listed as overruled because the change requirements cite them as the evidence of what is removed.

conflicts.about: Where the address book is kept: the prototype holds it in one user's session; the real book is persisted by the address book service and shared by the organisation.

positions.says: Additions, edits and deletions are held in the user's prototype session only.
No address book API is called; entries live in the session.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides it.
The book is scoped by organisation only, so every user of the organisation sees and changes the same book.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling's persistence constraint wins: the book stays persisted in the address book service and organisation-wide. The prototype's session-only storage is set aside; what the user sees on each page is still the prototype's.

conflicts.about: Whether the address view page shows addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses).

positions.says: The view page shows any address the service knows by id, looking in the book and then consignment, contact and transporter addresses.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as cross-service behaviour, overrides it.
The view page reads the address book service only, and anything it does not hold is not found.

conflicts.outcome: The cross-service constraint wins: a notification's addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only. How a notification shows its own addresses belongs to the journey areas.

conflicts.about: The row's View link: the prototype's bare 'View' against the real list's 'View <name>' with the name visually hidden.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
Each row ends with a 'View' link.
Each row's action is a link named 'View <the record's name>'.

conflicts.outcome: Sighted users see the same 'View' either way. The hidden name meets the accessibility regulations the service must satisfy (distinct link purpose for screen reader users), a real constraint a visual prototype does not express, so it is kept. Nothing is overruled: the prototype's View link is built.

conflicts.about: The service navigation's items: the prototype shows Dashboard, Templates, Address book and Manage account; the INS navigation also has Log out and no Templates.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as authentication, overrides it.
The navigation shows Dashboard, Templates, Address book and Manage account.
The navigation shows a Log out link to /auth/sign-out.

conflicts.outcome: Signing out is an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, so Log out stays. The prototype wins on the rest: Address book is the active item on its pages here, and the Templates item is the shared layout area's change. Nothing is overruled.

conflicts.about: The names of the list's query parameters: the prototype carries the tab in a 'category' parameter with values such as origin-and-consignor; Sam's 9 October ruling leaves the tab parameter, its values and the search parameter to the INS service.

positions.says: For the address book tabs and search, the tab parameter and its values, and the search parameter q, are the INS service's to name.
The selected tab comes from the category query parameter, origin-and-consignor when missing or unknown.
The filter form carries the selected tab as a hidden field named category.
The tab is addressed by an addressType parameter whose four values are ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR, DESTINATION_CONSIGNEE_OR_IMPORTER, TRANSPORTER and BRANCH, and the search stays q.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the INS service names the tab parameter and its values, which it has done as addressType with its own four values, and the search parameter keeps q. The prototype still decides the tabs, their order, the default tab and that the form keeps the tab, so its claims stay cited for that look and feel and nothing is overruled. Acceptance criteria assert the tab shown, not a literal query string.

conflicts.about: Which component draws the address book's category tabs: the prototype's GOV.UK tabs markup against the Ministry of Justice sub navigation Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling names.

positions.says: The category tabs are MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page, with the INS frontend adding the MoJ package.
The list page is built from GOV.UK button, tabs, table, pagination, select and input components plus custom pieces.
The tabs are links inside a navigation named 'Address types', with the tab being shown marked as the current page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the tabs are MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the list on that tab, and the INS frontend adds @ministryofjustice/frontend at the animals frontend's major version (req-1123), which the built list already renders as a named navigation of links. The prototype still decides the tab names, order and default. Its claim is not overruled because it also records the GOV.UK button, table, pagination, select and input components that are built as drawn.

conflicts.about: Whether the delete success banner re-cases the address's name to sentence case.

positions.says: The banner capitalises the name's first letter and lower-cases the rest.
The driving spec pins the sentence case, asserting 'Green valley farm address deleted'.
The banner names the address exactly as it is stored.
The banner is asserted as '<name> address deleted' against the record's own name, so it pins no case.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. The prototype wins on copy, so the banner's wording is adopted either way, but lower-casing the rest of a name the user typed changes how their own data is shown, and the prototype's reason for it is not visible: its demonstration names are all Title Case, where the result reads acceptably, while the real book holds names such as 'Alpine Dairy GmbH' that it would mangle. The built banner's assertion is templated on the record's name, so nothing settles it.
conflicts.question: Should the address book's delete banner lower-case the rest of the address's name, so 'Alpine Dairy GmbH' reads 'Alpine dairy gmbh'?
conflicts.default: The banner shows the name as the user entered it.

conflicts.about: What the 'Filter addresses' disclosure does when the list loads with a search or Type already applied.

positions.says: The filter sits inside a details element whose summary reads 'Filter addresses'.
The disclosure is collapsed when the list loads and the search field is hidden until the user opens it; typing filters in the browser, so the page never loads with a filter already applied.
The list's Search field is hidden until the 'Filter addresses' disclosure is opened, and nothing records what it does when the request already carries a search or a role.

conflicts.outcome: Left open. Once the filter is submitted to the server, 'collapsed when the list loads' can be read two ways and they build different pages. Always collapsed hides the term and role the shown results rest on, which no source asks for; open when a filter is applied keeps the prototype's uncluttered first load and still shows the user what they filtered by. Nothing in the rulings or the prototype ranks the two readings, because the prototype never reloads a filtered list, and the built list is only ever driven from a collapsed start.
conflicts.question: On the address book list, is the 'Filter addresses' disclosure open when the request carries a search or a Type, or collapsed whatever the request carries?
conflicts.default: It is open when the request carries a search or a Type, and collapsed otherwise.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's role-scoped list is served unpaginated, so a frontend reads the whole book and pages it for display, or is paged by the API itself.

positions.says: Every address book list and every address picker pages, no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated, and the list endpoint does take roles and does page, so the premise behind the unpaginated reading is no longer true of the service.
The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated, because the list endpoint takes no role: each frontend reads the whole book, filters by role itself and pages what is left for display.
The address-book service is asked for one role and gets an unpaginated list.
The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination, the list API paging with page and pageSize, and no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built.
Asking the address book API for a tab's roles returns exactly the addresses holding any of them.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's ruling of 25 November wins, and Paul's point 8 stands in full: every list of an organisation's addresses is served and shown a page at a time, and the role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong (req-address-book-list-001, req-address-book-list-002). The 23 November reading that the role-scoped list stays unpaginated, and the earlier instruction to ask for one role and take an unpaginated list, are set aside: they rested on a list endpoint that took no role, which the service no longer has.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's list can be asked for more than one role at once, which decides whether a category tab can be served by one request.

positions.says: Neither frontend can ask the address book for two roles at once, because the role predicate takes a single role.
The list endpoint takes roles and searchRoles alongside the page and the page size.
The address book list takes a role parameter, which is repeatable and matches any of the roles given, and a searchRole parameter.
Asking the address book API for a tab's roles returns exactly the addresses holding any of them.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's rulings of 5 and 25 November win: the list takes the roles an address must hold, repeatable and matching any of them, plus the roles a search is widened by, so one request serves a whole tab (req-address-book-list-002, req-1130). The 16 November observation that only a single role can be asked for described an earlier address book and is set aside; it is not a reason to read a whole category's pages client-side.

conflicts.about: Whether one address can be listed on more than one category tab.

positions.says: An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types, so an address with several types can appear on more than one tab.
The same place can be held twice in the address book under different uses, once as a place of origin and once as a consignor.
The address book refuses an address whose roles come from more than one group, and each role belongs to exactly one group.
